en: Mercury is the only metal that remains completely liquid at standard room temperature.
When iron rusts, it actually gains weight because it chemically bonds with oxygen from the air.
Diamonds and the soft graphite in your pencil are both made entirely of the exact same carbon atoms.
The metal gallium melts at 29.7 degrees Celsius, meaning it turns into a liquid puddle just by holding it in your warm hand.
Honey is a supersaturated solution containing so much dissolved sugar that it naturally crystallizes over time if left undisturbed.
Water is one of the very few substances that expands and becomes less dense when it freezes into solid ice.
Solid carbon dioxide, known as dry ice, skips the liquid phase entirely and sublimates directly into a cold gas.
Red cabbage juice acts as a natural chemical indicator, turning bright pink in acidic solutions and green in basic ones.
Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals, requiring a massive 3,422 degrees Celsius of heat to turn into a liquid.
Mayonnaise is a stable emulsion where tiny droplets of liquid oil are permanently suspended in water using egg yolk as an emulsifier.
A mixture of cornstarch and water acts as a non-Newtonian fluid that behaves like a solid when punched but flows like a liquid when poured.
The glowing gas inside a neon sign is actually a state of matter called plasma, where atoms lose their electrons.
